evidence: Cic. Sest. 19 (Lewis & Short): quam terribilis aspectū!
terms.comment: From terreō: what strikes terror, in looks, sound or power.

evidence: Cic. Att. 14.4.1: horribile est quae loquantur, quae minitentur
terms.comment: What makes one shudder (horrēre); in Cicero’s letters and Catullus also simply “awful, very bad” (see terrible, very bad).
Properly of evil omen; so fearful, awful, and of people cruel (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: horribile est quae loquantur, quae minitentur.
phrases.english: it is terrible what they say, what they threaten.

phrases.latin: madidīs Notus ēvolat ālīs, terribilem piceā tēctus cālīgine vultum
phrases.english: the South Wind flies out on dripping wings, his terrible face veiled in pitch-black mist
things we don’t know frighten us more
